Shared-memory TPU fragment reassembly, slot management, and mcache publish logic.

# Purpose
`fd_tpu_reasm.c` implements the shared-memory reassembly object used by the TPU transaction path. It defines the object life cycle functions [`fd_tpu_reasm_align`](<#fd_tpu_reasm_align>), [`fd_tpu_reasm_footprint`](<#fd_tpu_reasm_footprint>), [`fd_tpu_reasm_new`](<#fd_tpu_reasm_new>), [`fd_tpu_reasm_join`](<#fd_tpu_reasm_join>), [`fd_tpu_reasm_leave`](<#fd_tpu_reasm_leave>), [`fd_tpu_reasm_delete`](<#fd_tpu_reasm_delete>), and [`fd_tpu_reasm_reset`](<#fd_tpu_reasm_reset>). These functions validate the requested `depth` and `burst` values, lay out the shared memory region, create the internal hash map, and initialize the slot arrays and free-list state. The file also stores and checks the object `magic` value so callers can detect invalid joins or deleted objects.

The file also provides the main reassembly operations for transaction fragments. [`fd_tpu_reasm_query`](<#fd_tpu_reasm_query>) finds an active slot by `conn_uid` and `stream_id`. [`fd_tpu_reasm_prepare`](<#fd_tpu_reasm_prepare>) allocates a slot for a new stream and inserts it into the lookup map. [`fd_tpu_reasm_frag`](<#fd_tpu_reasm_frag>) appends fragment data into the slot buffer with size and offset checks. [`fd_tpu_reasm_publish`](<#fd_tpu_reasm_publish>) and [`fd_tpu_reasm_publish_fast`](<#fd_tpu_reasm_publish_fast>) write the completed transaction into `mcache`, update the publication ring, and free the oldest published slot. [`fd_tpu_reasm_cancel`](<#fd_tpu_reasm_cancel>) removes an active slot and returns it to the free list. The code uses `fd_dcache`, `fd_mcache`, and internal slot and map helpers to manage shared memory state and publication order.
